entities.summary: Henri II de Rohan, Duke of Rohan and Prince of Léon, was a key figure in the Huguenot movement, emerging in the tumultuous landscape of 17th-century France. As a Breton-French soldier and leader of the Huguenots, he played a pivotal role in shaping the fate of this minority group. Born into a noble family in 1605, Henri II de Rohan ascended to the dukedom of Rohan in 1626, becoming a prominent leader in the struggle for Huguenot rights. His leadership during the Wars of Religion, particularly his role in the siege of La Rochelle in 1628, garnered significant attention from European powers. However, his efforts ultimately proved unsuccessful, and he was forced to flee France in 1628. Despite this, Henri II de Rohan's legacy as a champion of the Huguenots endured, influencing the course of French history and cementing his place as a notable figure in the annals of European history. He died on April 13, 1638, without any children, leaving behind a lasting impact on the region. His story is a testament to the complexities of 17th-century European politics and the ongoing struggles for religious tolerance.
